::: {.at-a-glance}
- **Time:** 10 minutes.
- **Before you start:** everything you want to keep is pushed to GitHub (`git status` is clean, `git log origin/main` shows your commits). Deleting a project folder deletes its Git history too.
:::

## How much space did the course take?

```{.bash .run}
pixi info | grep -i "cache"
```

```{.bash .norun}
du -sh ~/cbio7501/*
```

On our test laptop: about 3.6 GB of environments for the LTEE project, 0.5 GB
of data and results, and several GB in Pixi's shared package cache.

## 1. Project environments

Each project keeps its environments in its own `.pixi/` folder. Remove them;
`pixi install` rebuilds them from `pixi.lock` whenever you need them again:

```{.bash .norun}
cd ~/cbio7501/ltee-project
pixi clean
```

Do the same in your capstone project and in the practice folders
(`pixi-practice`, `conda-comparison/from-conda`).

## 2. Workflow and analysis leftovers

Everything here is rebuilt by `pixi run reproduce`:

```{.bash .norun}
cd ~/cbio7501/ltee-project
rm -rf results/* data/processed/* .snakemake work .nextflow .nextflow.log*
```

Keep `results/README.md` and `data/processed/README.md` (they are committed;
`git status` shows if you deleted them, and `git restore` brings them back).

## 3. Pixi's package cache

All projects share one cache of downloaded packages. Emptying it frees the most
space; the next `pixi install` downloads again:

```{.bash .norun}
pixi clean cache
```

Lesson 05b also used micromamba, which has its own cache:
`pixi exec micromamba clean --all --yes`.

## 4. Global tools and Pixi itself

```{.bash .run}
pixi global list
```

```{.bash .norun}
pixi global uninstall cookiecutter
```

To remove Pixi completely (from the Pixi documentation's uninstall steps):
empty the cache (step 3), clean your workspaces (step 1), then

```{.bash .norun}
rm -r ~/.pixi
```

and delete the line that adds `~/.pixi/bin` to your `PATH` in `~/.bashrc` or
`~/.zshrc` (on Windows, remove `%UserProfile%\.pixi\bin` from the `PATH`
environment variable).

## 5. Docker

Images take a lot of space. Remove what you no longer need:

```{.bash .norun}
docker image ls
docker image rm ltee-project:0.1.0
docker system prune          # stopped containers, unused networks, build cache; read the prompt
```

To uninstall Docker Desktop, use its *Troubleshoot → Uninstall* menu (macOS,
Windows) or your package manager (Linux).

## 6. Codespaces

Codespaces count against your monthly storage quota while they exist, even when
stopped. Delete the ones you do not need at <https://github.com/codespaces>.

## What to keep

- Your GitHub repositories (`ltee-project`, your capstone): they are your
  portfolio and the record of your work.
- Your Zenodo records: they cannot be deleted anyway, which is the point.
- `pixi.toml` and `pixi.lock` in every project: with them, everything above
  comes back with one command.

## Further reading

- Pixi documentation, *Installation* (includes uninstalling): <https://pixi.prefix.dev/latest/installation/>
- Docker documentation, *Prune unused Docker objects*: <https://docs.docker.com/engine/manage-resources/pruning/>
